scope: Three frontends use one CRT-free implementation for subscription lists, event filtering, coalesced reentrancy, retry and callback lifetime. Each loaded frontend module owns its hook/message worker; callbacks synchronize with removal using the process transport lock, retain no API object pointer across callbacks, and unhook on the installing worker. Worker module references, duplicated startup-ready handles, atomic lock publication and generation checks protect concurrent shutdown/restart. Present and report capture/queueing are serialized against event callbacks; D3D9 releases the lock around window activation and recaptures after reacquiring it. This fixes deterministic stale-window ordering regressions in all three production Present functions without claiming an atomic Win32/GDI snapshot. Real XP creates 12 objects per API, validates the twelfth with 22 independent Win32 observations while neither presenting after actions nor pumping application messages, produces 136 reports, and unloads all three DLLs after final release. New trace passes SwiftShader/Metal surface replay; previous two window fixtures pass their SwiftShader entry points. Four fresh browser runs are reported separately from the unchanged 4G2 full 44-run/533-pixel host baseline. No native Microsoft D3D8/9 drawing or game/FPS acceptance claim. Remaining retail API semantics, guest wrappers, programmable CPU processing and stages 5/6 continue.
